variants.display_name: PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 · vLLM · Batch 4 · Regions shared across GPUs
variants.change_description: vs batch 1: batch four regions per GPU and share regions across all GPUs. Fresh NACA and Census studies motivate embedding precision and OCR scheduling next.

outcome_note.summary: Sharing regions across GPUs reduced p50 to 5.39 s: 2.80× the batch 1 baseline.
outcome_note.next: NACA spends 35.5% in embedding; Census has a long OCR tail. Test BF16 embeddings, then page and region scheduling.

experiment.name: paddleocr_vllm_five_pdf_eval
experiment.title: PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 · vLLM · Five-PDF evaluation
experiment.hardware_note: 4 NVIDIA L4 GPUs · 22.5 GiB GPU memory each · 72 W per GPU · AMD EPYC 7R13, 96 logical CPUs · 363 GiB RAM

quality.summary: All 15 added pages produced nonempty Markdown and every recognition region ended with raw EOS. Page output, form sections, captions and beginnings/endings were inspected; the two prior references remain unchanged.

cases.review_context: Retained unchanged from the earlier accepted reference set; five-repeat validation pending.

known_limitations: Native parser Markdown preserves some charts and diagrams as image references rather than transcribing plotted data. These placeholders are part of the frozen output contract.
OCR has ordinary recognition and table-structure errors; reference agreement measures repeatability and optimization fidelity, not character-perfect source accuracy.
quality.quality_fix: Shared table-image limit of 2,822,400 pixels; greedy decoding and EOS checks unchanged.
